reflection: Volume-contrast factors dominate the notebook: they help in 2023 and 2025 and lose in 2022 and 2024, and the team now has three of them. Price-based and sign-based factors (overnight, sign consistency, signed gaps) were rejected, so they add noise. The R15 team joiners were the vol-scaled variants, which suggests that scaling by a volatility regime reduces the 2024 losses. This round I will try volume contrasts with other normalizers (a ratio of short to long QQQ volatility, MSFT as a baseline), and a few new angles that are not simple volume z-scores: a price-volume interaction using range expansion, and a volume-trend acceleration. I will also add partners that combine QQQ volume divergence with Apple-specific relative state.

lessons.name: qqq_volume_move_divergence_vol_regime_gated
lessons.lesson: Dividing QQQ volume-vs-move divergence by QQQ's 20d volatility damped high-vol stretches and made it a team member, though 2022 and 2024 still lacked gains.

lessons.name: aapl_vs_qqq_volume_surge_vs_vol_ratio
lessons.lesson: Multiplying the AAPL-vs-QQQ volume gap by Apple's short/long volatility ratio gave an interaction that helped all four years on the team, so conditioning on a volatility regime adds real information.

lessons.name: aapl_overnight_vs_intraday_20d
lessons.lesson: Smoothed overnight versus intraday drift is a slow price pattern with no volume context and it hurt both models, especially in 2024.

lessons.name: aapl_return_sign_consistency_10d
lessons.lesson: Sign-count differences throw away magnitude and mostly repeat existing return-mean factors, so they added only noise.

lessons.name: qqq_range_expansion_x_aapl_volume_gap
lessons.lesson: As written it was only QQQ range expansion, with no real volume gap term, so it was a plain volatility-state proxy that hurt in 2022, 2024 and 2025.

lessons.name: aapl_minus_qqq_return_x_volume_gap_signed
lessons.lesson: Multiplying a sign by the volume gap made a binary-flipping feature that overfit and lost in 3 of 4 years, so direction-signed volume does not work here.

factors.name: qqq_volume_move_divergence_vol_ratio_gated
factors.hypothesis: The parent lost in 2024 and 2022 because the divergence signal matters mainly when short-term volatility is rising. Multiplying by QQQ's 5d/60d volatility ratio, which worked for the Apple version, should emphasize those episodes.

factors.name: aapl_vs_msft_volume_surge_vs_vol_ratio
factors.hypothesis: Using MSFT volume as the baseline instead of QQQ gives a mega-cap comparison that is less correlated with the QQQ factors on the team, while keeping the volatility-ratio gate that gave 4/4 years.

factors.name: aapl_volume_acceleration_vs_range_trend
factors.hypothesis: Apple volume building over a week without a matching range expansion indicates quiet accumulation or distribution. This differs from the single-day z-scores already tried.

factors.name: qqq_short_vs_long_vol_x_aapl_beta_gap
factors.hypothesis: When market volatility is elevated, Apple's 10d relative drift versus QQQ may mean-revert or persist differently than in calm periods. This is a price-based regime interaction, not another volume z-score.

factors.name: aapl_range_scaled_qqq_volume_gap_vs_msft
factors.hypothesis: The team's QQQ divergence factor describes market stress. This Apple-vs-MSFT volume gap, scaled by the same QQQ volatility regime, describes Apple's relative attention within that regime and should add something on top of it.

factors.name: msft_volume_vs_price_divergence_range_scaled
factors.hypothesis: The QQQ volume-vs-move divergence worked as a market factor. The same construction on MSFT gives a peer-lead version that complements Apple's own range-scaled volume contrast.
